articleTitle: Hexa Cell Triangular CSRR for the Non Invasive Detection of Blood Glucose
abstract: The authors propose a compact metamaterial microwave sensor named the Hexa Cell Triangular Complementary Split-ring Resonator (HC-TCSRR), sized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60\times 20 \times 1.5\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>, designed for non-invasive monitoring of blood glucose levels ranging from 50 to 1000 mg/dL. This unique structure is novel in this application. The theoretical analysis and numerical modelling of the HC-TCSRR sensor were conducted using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software. When the sensor's sensitivity was demonstrated through simulation in the range of 70–1000 mg/dL, the results exhibited a distinct leftward frequency shift in the transmission response. The sensor showed a maximum sensitivity of up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13.35 \times 10^{-2}\text{dB}/(\text{mg}/\text{dL})$</tex> and 4.53 MHz/(mg/dL) in simulations. In vitro tests using deionized aqueous glucose solutions (50–200 mg/dL) also showed a left shifts in the resonant frequency of the transmission response. The fabricated HC-TCSRR prototype achieved a maximum sensitivity of 10.24 MHz /(mg/dL). To the best of our knowledge, distinct frequency shifts at lower glucose concentrations (70, 100, 120 mg/dL) and high concentration of 1000 mg/dL with the same sensor have not been reported till now. Furthermore, with its affordability, compact size, operational versatility across various glucose concentrations, and enhanced sensitivity, this sensor concept is a promising candidate for wearable non-invasive continuous blood glucose monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Microwave Sensor for Precise Temperature Detection in Phosphate Materials
abstract: This study presents a sensor design with a single notch resonating around 2 GHz, aimed at simulating the effect of phosphate temperature on the sensor's response. The sensor consists of a centrally positioned resonator coupled with two 50-ohm transmission lines, a configuration chosen to enhance sensitivity and selectivity to temperature changes. Simulated on a Rogers 5880 substrate with a thickness of 0.789 mm, the sensor resonates at a specific frequency, making it highly sensitive to phosphate temperature variations. Simulations were performed to assess the sensor's ability to determine phosphate temperatures ranging from 25°C to 60°C by measuring the frequency shift of unheated phosphate as a reference and comparing it to the shifts observed in heated samples. The results indicate a clear frequency shift corresponding to temperature changes, demonstrating the sensor's potential for accurate phosphate temperature measurement.

articleTitle: Boosting Microwave Hydration Sensors Performance with Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This study introduces innovative non-invasive hydration microwave sensors combined with machine learning (ML) algorithms for monitoring purposes. Specifically, a miniaturized complementary-split ring resonator (CSRR) operating in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\div 3$</tex> GHz band for assessing human skin hydration through near-field interaction, and a separate patch antenna operating at 2.45 GHz for tracking the drying process of greenwood. The design process involves full-wave simulations to evaluate the resonators and patch antenna capability to effectively penetrate skin layers and wood structures. After fabrication on cost-effective substrates, extensive testing measurements were conducted on different mediums. Human volunteers' proximal wrist areas are monitored over six days with multiple daily measurements under various dietary conditions. Concurrently, the greenwood sample is assessed over twenty days in a controlled climate chamber. The spectral data obtained from the resonator and the patch antenna are analyzed using advanced multivariate data analysis (MVDA). The results confirm the method's effectiveness in accurately categorizing hydration levels and emphasize its potential for practical hydration monitoring applications due to its cost-effectiveness and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Enhanced Permittivity Measurement Using a High-Sensitivity Microwave Sensor Based on Split Ring Resonators
abstract: In this paper, a low profile and high sensitivity metamaterial microwave sensor for dielectric materials characterization is presented. The proposed sensor consists of one split ring resonator (SRR) in microstrip technology, printed on Rogers 5880 substrate. The SRR is placed between two microstrip line instead of indirect coupling which concentrate the electric field in the sensing area, hence increasing the sensitivity. The sensing mechanism is based on measuring the change of the minimum transmission frequency produced by different dielectric properties of the loaded materials under test (MUTs). This proposed design exhibits a high sensitivity close to 54 % as the relative permittivity of MUTs changes from 1 to 10. To the best of authour's knowledge, this is the highest sensitivity obtain up to now using SRR based sensor. The permittivity derivation is validated experimentally by measuring well known materials, specially Polylactic acid (PLA), FR-4 epoxy and ROTMMI0i. The developed sensor is cost effective and can be suitable for several applications including nondestructive, microfluidics and biomedical sensors.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Rogowski Coil to Measure Fast Current of MARX Generator
abstract: In this work, the analytical design, simulation, and experimental verification of a Rogowski coil for the diagnostic of a Marx Generator output current is presented. The proposed Rogowski coil is designed based on geometry constraint of the Marx Generator structure and its generated electrical pulse. Furthermore, the presented sensor will include geometrical design and frequency response analysis, to measure currents in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kA}$</tex> amplitude and MHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Cross-Shaped Slot UWB Miniature Patch Antennas for 28 GHz 5G mmWave Applications Using ANN Based on k-Fold Cross-Validation
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for designing and optimizing an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) patch antenna utilizing an Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The main objective is to accurately predict the essential dimensions of the patch antenna to meet specific resonance and bandwidth requirements, thereby streamlining the design process. The ANN model is rigorously trained and validated using the k-fold cross-validation method, ensuring robust performance and accurate predictions across multiple data subsets. The results demonstrate that the ANN model can precisely forecast the dimensions of the patch antenna, achieving a resonance frequency of 28 GHz and a bandwidth of 20 GHz. The proposed antenna exhibits a maximum gain of 5.75 dB and an efficiency of 99%, which is on par or better than existing designs. The effectiveness of the proposed model is further validated through simulations using HFSS and CST software, showing excellent agreement in reflection coefficient, gain, and efficiency.

articleTitle: Self-Attenuating Graphene-Based Antennas Utilizing Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) Substrates
abstract: In this study, a Terahertz (THz) band antenna which can regulate its own resonant frequency without the requirement of manual adjustment is simulated. A polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) substrate is applied onto a rectangular graphene patch antenna. With a voltage potential applied onto the PVDF, the patch antenna can attenuate its frequency by physically changing the shape of the antenna, and in turn its resonant frequency. These antennas are within a 0.1 THz band between 1.32 THz to 1.22 THz measured from a radial bend of a flat surface to r = 75 μm, fitting into a return loss (S11) above -30 dB. Although the return loss did not show consistency, the resonating frequency shifted at a linear rate relative to the cylindrical bending.

articleTitle: A Circularly/ Linearly Polarized Multiband Antenna with Alternating Split-Ring Resonators for Wireless Applications
abstract: This research presents a dipole antenna design that uses metamaterials to obtain a multiband device for advanced wireless applications. The antenna has overall electrical dimensions of 36.6×140×0.5<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mm</inf>3 and is printed on a Rogers RT 5870 substrate. By incorporating split-ring resonator array with an alternative arrangement to the dipole antenna, a circularly polarized multiband antenna with high gain, excellent impedance matching and high efficiency is achieved. This metamaterial antenna operates at various frequencies, including 0.9-1GHz, 2.34-2.48GHz, 3.32-3.43GHz, 4.57-4.69GHz, 5.12-5.24GHz, and 5.93-6.11GHz, making it suitable for a wide range of applications, including RFID, WLAN, WiMAX, Wi-Fi 6/6E, and 5G NR. The proposed structure features low profile, easy integration into electrical circuits, and low-cost fabrication, making it a suitable option for various wireless systems.

articleTitle: Optimized Microwave Ring-Gap Resonator for Microchannel Particules State Monitoring
abstract: This paper presents a study on a highly sensitive microwave sensor designed for the detection of a single yeast bioparticle. The sensor design integrates a planar microwave annular ring-gap resonator, coupled with a microfluidic channel for precise bioparticle manipulation. To optimize field confinement and maximize electric field strength, a small gap has been introduced into the resonator. This approach holds great potential for various applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Phase Optimization on the Cascade Channel and System Performance of RIS-Assisted Wireless Networks
abstract: In this work, we investigate the impacts of the Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) phases or reflection matrix on the effective cascade (i.e., joint transmitter (TX)-to-RIS and RIS-to-receiver (RX)) channel and on the system performance for RIS-aided wireless networks. Using channel gain, signal-to-noise ratio and spectral efficiency as metrics, we demonstrate that our physical model-based RIS phases employing an optimized Fourier Transform (FT)-based beam-forming algorithm outperforms the cosine similarity (CS) phase algorithm. Unlike the CS algorithm where the RIS phases are deduced from the joint incident and reflected channel vectors, the optimized FT-based phases are blind to the cascade channels. We benchmark our results with random RIS phases as well as the mathematical upper bound. The results show that the FT phases outperform the CS and random phases, and approach the mathematical upper bound performance under diverse system parameters and configurations.

articleTitle: Vector Modulator Based Low RMS Phase Error Phase Shifter for Ka-Band Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a Vector Modulator type phase shifter operating in the Ka-band. This system is based on an I/Q hybrid transformer that feeds a vector modulator, which adjusts the amplitude of quadrature differential signals. A specially designed passive attenuator enhances attenuation depth, phase accuracy, and impedance matching. A 55nm CMOS circuit was simulated, achieving a 360° phase shift with 5.6° resolution and exhibiting an RMS phase error of less than 2°. The designed phase shifter occupies a total area of 0.22 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and its reflection coefficient remains below −10 dB across different bias conditions It spans the frequency range from 25 to 27 GHz, paving the way for high data rate mobile millimeter-wave telecommunication systems

articleTitle: Reducing Mutual Coupling Using Ring SRR MetaSurface for Multiband MIMO Antenna
abstract: This work reduces mutual coupling in a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna system by using two circular SRR meta-surface (MS) walls. The array of two-by-one rectangular patches is oriented normally and placed between the horizontal plane and the meta-surfacestructures. The proposed array is simulated using the CST studio software. The outcome outputs illustrate the effects of applying the meta-surface wall. By using the proposed MS barriers, mutual coupling is reduced.

articleTitle: Flexible Passive UHF RFID Tag for the Identification of Blood Bags and Intravenous Solutions
abstract: This paper presents a flexible UHF RFID tag made of copper printed on kapton polyimide substrate. This tag is double-layered with the radiation plane printed on one kapton substrate and the ground plane printed on the other kapton substrate. It has a compact size of volume 50 × 20 × 0.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>whose flexibility makes it easier to label complex surfaces. The proposed tag is designed for applications in the medical field, notably for the identification of blood bags and Intra-Veinous (IV) solutions. It helps prevent misidentification of samples based on their characteristics. It adapts very well to the Monza R6 chip <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Z_{c}=13-j125\Omega)$</tex> at 868 MHz when applied to a blood bag as well as an IV solution bag. Simulation results show good performance in terms of adaptation and reading range. The tag is fabricated and measurements are done on a foam surface, because surfaces used in simulations, we are not available in the laboratory. Measurements and simulations results on foam are consistent, so it's highly likely that the same results will be obtained with blood and IV solution bags. The maximum reading range is 2 m at 868 MHz.

articleTitle: Ku-Band Groove-Gap-Waveguide Dual-Band Bandpass Filter With Multi-Transmission-Zero Sharp-Rejection Transfer Function
abstract: A high-selectivity dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) in groove-gap-waveguide (GGW) technology for Ku-band application is presented. It consists of a third-order GGW-cavity-resonator dual-band BPF block arranged in a split-type configuration with an additional oversized cavity inserted at its input access. The dual-band BPF block exhibits a third-order filtering response with three inter-band transmission zeros (TZs), while two more TZs between passbands and several TZs below/above the lower/upper passbands are produced by the input reactive load. In this manner, an overall sharp-rejection dual-band BPF response with multiple TZs being generated by two different mecha-nisms that avoid cross couplings is obtained. The RF operational principles and design foundations of the devised GGW dual-band BPF are detailed. Moreover, for practical-validation purposes, a proof-of-concept prototype corresponding to a 13.7/16-GHz dual-band BPF design example is manufactured and characterized.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent 4-Port UWB Antenna for MIMO Applications
abstract: Herein, we present a novel transparent antenna with ultra-wideband (UWB) performance along with polarization diversity through 4 ports allowing MIMO operation. The antenna design can be of a great interest for a vehicular applications and Internet of Things (IOT) where the dual polarization and multiple ports allows as well as medical glasses and vehicular windows where transparency is needed for visibility. The proposed antenna provides compact size with dimensions of 50 mm×50 mm, through the employment of CPW, dual orthogonal-polarization, isolation level of 20 dB, and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) of 0.0016 as well as MIMO performance.

articleTitle: SLL Suppression Performance of the Blackman Linear Array Antenna
abstract: The development of power-weighted method on the array antenna is dominated by using window function as weighting coefficient. One of the window functions that has been rarely implemented on the power-weighted method but has a very promising chance of sidelobe level (SLL) suppression capabilities is Blackman function. The average of SLL suppression on a linear array antenna using a popular weighting such as Chebyshev is 25 dB, whereas the Blackman function is theoretically capable of delivering an SLL suppression performance of more than 25 dB. This paper presents the modelling and application of power-weighted method with Blackman function as weighting coefficient on the design of a linear array antenna, namely Blackman linear array (BLA). It is demonstrated that on the 1 × 8 BLA design, SLL suppression can deliver maximum output to eliminate sidelobes with the suppression level reaching 39.14 dB to 42.70 dB. While front to back ratio (FTBR) parameter, the proposed 1 × 8 BLA has the value of 13.44 dB. In addition, the comparison of radiation patterns produced by the BLA and with the uniform linear array (ULA) is also reported.

articleTitle: A 2.4GHz Electrically Small Antenna for IoT Terminals
abstract: A low-cost planar Electrically Small Antenna (ESA) for narrow-band IoT terminals is presented. The ESA is based on a loop whose first anti-resonance is utilized for impedance matching. Its excitation mechanism reinforces its magnetic mode while suppressing its electric dipole modes to achieve an end-fire omni-directional pattern. A 2.4GHz prototype is designed and simulated. It achieves excellent return loss with 53% total radiation efficiency at 2.445GHz. An active prototype is also designed where the ESA is fed by a chip oscillator.

articleTitle: Innovative Design of a Compact Diplexer Using Heterogeneous Filters for 5G and WiMAX
abstract: The rapid advancement of wireless communication systems, such as 5G and WiMAX, demands compact, efficient, and high-performance diplexers that can operate effectively at multiple frequency bands. This necessitates their miniaturization without compromising performance. This paper presents the design of a miniaturized microstrip diplexer using heterogeneous bandpass filters (BPFs) and a coupled junction, on a Rogers RT/Duroid 5870 substrate. The ADS electromagnetic simulator was used to characterize the frequency responses of the proposed diplexer. It exhibits satisfactory isolation, in excess of 40 dB over the entire operating frequency band from 3.5 to 5.2 GHz. Additionally, insertion losses in the passband are less than 0.8 dB, the diplexer also achieves return losses of approximately 28 dB and 12.8 dB for the two respective channels. Additionally, the overall size of the presented diplexer measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${21} \times {15}\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. These findings validate that the proposed diplexer is highly suitable for 5G and WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: Dual Channel C-Band Solid State Power Amplifier for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents the architecture of a Dual Channel C-Band Solid State Power Amplifier (SSPA) for a Dual-mode and Multi carrier operation with integrated monitor and control sections for airborne applications such as data communication link for medium altitude long endurance Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). This paper details about the ability of the SSPA to independently amplify two carrier signals simultaneously with different gains using high power GaN devices at the final amplifying stage and then combining them using a directional coupler to radiate both amplified signals from a single Antenna. In this design a micro-controller based monitor and control circuitry is used to provide protection against High temperature, High output VSWR, Input Over drive and Input over-voltage. This SSPA operates in the C band for a single 28V DC supply while delivering greater than 41.5dBm linear power and gain greater than 45dB. This module is realized on a 10 layer hybrid PCB using PTFE and FR4 laminates without compromising on performance.

articleTitle: A Multi-Bistatic UGV-GPR System for Increased Surveyed Area Coverage
abstract: This paper presents the concept and implementation of a Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) front end integrated with an Ultra- Wideband multi-antenna system for enhanced surveyed area coverage. The proposed radiating unit comprises an UWB RF switch capable of sequentially selecting 1 out of 8 Tx-Rx antenna pairs. The GPR-Antenna system is mounted on an unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) so that the presented configuration increases the covered area in a single UGV-GPR pass. One of the key advantages of the system is its ability to align multiple B-scans in one run, which facilitates the identification of buried targets.

articleTitle: Characterization of Microwave Magneto-Dielectric Antenna Incorporating Yttrium Iron Garnet
abstract: This paper addresses the characterization of magneto-dielectric (MD) antenna by incorporating ferrite material, namely Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG), which operates at microwave frequencies. The YIG is intended to be incorporated within the dielectric material to construct an MD-antenna. The antenna configuration takes a square-shaped patch arranged directly upon the ferrite material, with an FR-4 Epoxy substrate applied as the host dielectric material. This study examines the effect of a bulk circular-shaped YIG inclusion inside the antenna without applying an external magnetic bias. The characterization results show the higher-order resonance mode at the frequency of 4.45 GHz, while the conventional patch antenna resonates at the fundamental mode of at the frequency of 3.78 GHz.

articleTitle: X-Band High Power Compact Octal Transmit/Receive Module
abstract: This paper conveys the design of an Octal Transmit-Receive Module (OTRM) functional in X-Band for ground and surveillance radar applications. This illustrates the realization of an optimized module solution using a single composite multi-layer PCB design. The main highlight of this approach is to achieve high transmit power (i.e >44dBm) per channel in a very compact size along with efficient thermal management. Gallium Nitride (GaN) based main power amplifier has been used to achieve high power and efficiency. The module functions on discrete power supplies with inbuilt monitoring, controlling and sequencing circuit. Combination of Field-programmable gate array (FPGA) based control circuitry and timing of the pulsing circuitry enhances the switching rate between transmit and receive operation. Advanced and effective mechanical design fulfills the thermal requirement without any compromise in electrical performance. The developed OTRM delivers high transmit power (>44 dBm), low noise figure (<4dB) and the required receive gain with a proper heat dissipation mechanism.

Author Keywords: Gallium Nitride high transmit power and FPGA

articleTitle: Reflective Metasurface Based on Embroidered Meander Resonators
abstract: This paper presents a concept of reflecting meta-surface (MS) with a novel unit cell design utilizing embroidered meander resonators. The resonators are formed by a silver-coated nylon thread embroidered on a felt textile substrate and have resonant frequencies around 3 GHz. Numerical simulations and experiments with prototypes have demonstrated that the proposed MS elements have a high and relatively broadband reflection greater than -5 dB in the range 2–4 GHz. Moreover, their resonance frequency can be changed within the same range by modifying the meander arm length. Reflecting MS formed by such elements can be fixed easily on a wall of a house or a tent in urban or rural environments and used as a passive Reflective Intelligent Surface (RIS) to facilitate mobile communications in areas like mountains and deserts. To the best of our knowledge, this paper demonstrates a possibility to use a fully textile MS element for this purpose for the first time.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Multiband SIW Antenna Using the PSO Algorithm
abstract: In this work, we propose an innovative method for the design and optimization of a compact, multiband SIW antenna with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30 \times 20\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The antenna uses substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology and features two V-shaped resonators etched on its top surface. Optimization was carried out using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, programmed in MATLAB, which enhanced the antenna's performance. This approach enabled us to design a multiband SIW antenna capable of resonating in five narrow bands centered on the frequencies of 9 GHz, 10 GHz, 10.4 GHz, 13 GHz, and 14 GHz. These frequencies are particularly well-suited for applications in radar systems, satellite communications, and high-frequency data transmission, notably in the X-band (9 GHz-12 GHz) and Ku-band (12 GHz-18 GHz). Simulations indicate that the antenna achieves a maximum gain of 7.1 dBi, making it an excellent choice for radar and satellite communication systems in the specified frequency bands.

articleTitle: Moving Structures in a 3D FDTD Code
abstract: This paper introduces a method that combines the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique with a direct modeling approach to study electromagnetic field diffraction from moving 3D structures. By updating object positions after a specified number of time steps within the FDTD time-stepping loop, the method effectively models motion. Comprehensive descriptions of the theoretical foundation and algorithm are included. The method's effectiveness is illustrated through a case study involving the diffraction response of a moving metallic sphere illuminated by a line source.

articleTitle: 6-Port Rotationally Symmetric Antennas Supporting Orbital Angular Momentum Modes
abstract: The use of digital platforms with rapidly increasing users in the wireless domain leads communication systems to provide high data rates, reliability, and strong quality. In this context, Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antennas are getting more attention and play an essential part in the current generation of wireless technology. This work presents the performance of a 6-element rotationally symmetric MIMO antenna design based on a magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna approach to be used in advanced MIMO applications such as Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) and high-capacity channels. Cognitive wireless technologies for vehicular communications, combined with OAM modes, aim to enhance Non-Line-Of-Sight (NLOS) short-distance communications for smart mobility. Antenna compatibility with the OAM mode is derived from specific spherical vector harmonic function momentum tensors synthesized from the dipoles. An optimized design is presented with good agreement between numerical and experimental results for the operating frequency band of 4.0 to 5.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Minimizing Body Impact on Wearable Rectenna Performance for Energy Harvesting Using a Huygens Source
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of a new rectenna for wearable applications in the ISM band. The rectenna features a microstrip dipole antenna embroidered on the top surface of a felt textile substrate and connected by a Schottky diode rectifier. Additionally, a magnetic dipole is integrated on the bottom surface of the substrate to create a Huygens source, effectively reducing the impact of the human body on rectenna performance. The results demonstrate that with a very low input power (-15 dBm), the rectenna can increase the gain by 2.54 dBi at a frequency of 2.45 GHz and a distance of 5 mm from the body. Furthermore, the rectenna maintains a reflection coefficient (S11) below -25 dB across different bending radii, indicating its adaptability to body movements. The proposed rectenna is cost-effective, flexible, and suitable for both on-body and off-body applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Coupling and Bandwidth in MIMO System Antenna Based on Dielectric Resonator Antenna Using Meta-Surface
abstract: A two-cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) based multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system without and with the meta-surface to enhance the coupling mutual between them and the bandwidth is proposed in this paper. The two elements of the dielectric resonator antenna are close to each other by a distance of 0.06λo and alimented by the coaxial feed. The distance between the antenna elements and the meta-surface is 0.2λo. The simulation result showed the improvement of the coupling by 10dB and the bandwidth enhanced by 7% in the operation band frequency at center 2.85GHz by using the approach of meta-surface.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Indoor Localization Methods Using RFID Technology
abstract: With encouragement all over the world for the number of such applications in areas like healthcare systems, logistics, and inventory management, indoor localization using Radio Frequency Identification technology seems to be quite promising. It is against this background that this article discusses three leading methods of indoor localization and hence for this purpose: empirical indoor path loss model, LANDMARC model, and triangulation model. This paper aims to review these methods in the light of certain criteria, upon which would then help in deciding which of these methods are effective if any object is to be located accurately while at rest inside indoor environments. In this quest, advantages, disadvantages, and operational considerations related to each method have been broadly discussed to add valuable input to literature directed towards RFID-based indoor localization systems. Results of the comparative analysis show that the empirical model is very flexible and cost-effective compared to the triangulation, which gives high accuracy but needs a more complex implementation, the LANDMARC model is simple and precise but may be less adaptable to specific localization needs in different environments.

articleTitle: Study and Design of a Reliable Antenna Deployment System for Nanosatellites
abstract: This paper presents the study and design of a reliable antenna deployment system for nanosatellites, focusing on both mechanical and electrical aspects. Nanosatellites, particularly CubeSats, require efficient and reliable antenna deployment systems to ensure mission success. This study examines material selection, design considerations, and testing protocols to optimize the deployment system for nanosatellites in space environments. The proposed solution includes a deployment mechanism that ensures durability, reliability, and compatibility with the constraints of nanosatellite missions.

articleTitle: Stellar Aberration and Fizeau's experiment with Moving Water, Using the FDTD Method
abstract: This paper presents a full-wave analysis of Stellar aberration and the Fresnel-Lorentz drag effect using a direct finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, where the source, observer, and dielectric medium are all in motion. By updating object positions at specific intervals within the FDTD time-stepping loop, this approach effectively models motion.

articleTitle: A Design Methodology for a Dual-Mode Coplanar Waveguide Junction Circulator
abstract: Circulators with inherent multiband operation are beneficial to low-power and small form factor radars for emerging beamforming and remote sensing applications. In this paper, a design methodology for a dual-mode junction circulator on coplanar waveguide structure is presented. Several magnetic and geometric parameters are shown to have an impact on the standing wave pattern at the circulator junction. Contrasting circulation directions are obtained at the two resonant frequencies of 4.76 GHz and 8.54 GHz with a low insertion loss of 1–2 dB and isolation ratios better than 35 dB and 22 dB for the first and second order modes, respectively.

articleTitle: GaN/SiC Upper F-Band Single Ended Power Amplifier
abstract: This article presents the design implementation, analysis and performance of a four-stage single ended power amplifier (PA) developed on a 40 nm gallium nitride on silicon carbide (GaN/SiC) technology. The circuit targets the upper F-Band, and it operates from 125 GHz to 130 GHz. At 130 GHz, the amplifier aims to have a small signal power gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> of 18 dB, peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 10, and to achieve a saturated output power (PSat) of 27 dBm. Based on EM simulations this is the highest power level reported on this technology at the frequency of operation to date.

articleTitle: Polarization-Agile Antenna for Physiological Radar Monitoring Systems
abstract: In Doppler radar systems for human respiratory motion measurement, the change in wave polarization after reflection can be critical. In this contribution, a polarization-agile antenna based on a cavity-back slot fed by stripline is proposed to improve the experimental setup to investigate polarimetric effects in such measurements. The antenna consists of a series-fed sequentially-rotated array of four elements terminated in two ports. In this way, it is demonstrated that both right-handed and left-handed circular polarizations can be received and, by combination of both, arbitrary polarization can be obtained.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Low-Cost IoT Electrically Small Antenna
abstract: A Circularly Polarized (CP) Electrically Small An-tenna (ESA) is presented targeting low data-rate IoT applications. The antenna is based on a combination of a capacitively-loaded magnetic dipole generating a horizontally polarized field and a top-loaded electric dipole generating the vertically polarized orthogonal component. The antenna has an electrical size of 0.58rad at 2.48GHz. Its radiation pattern is omni-directional in the azimuth plane with a left-hand CP realized gain of -4.7dBi, an axial ratio lower than 3dB and a total radiation efficiency of 41%. This makes it suitable for use with the circuitry of IoT terminals that require 360 degrees spatial coverage with immunity to multi-path and polarization mismatch effects.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering by Elliptical Dielectric Cylinder Using the WCIP Method
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the distribution of the electromagnetic field near an infinite dielectric elliptical cylinder. The Waves Concept Iterative Process method is formulated in elliptical approach to address electromagnetic problems involving a dielectric elliptical cylinder. The proposed method is based on the introduction of incident and reflected waves tangential to the elliptical surface. These waves are defined by a linear relationship between the electric field and the current density. A spectral reflexion operators relating the incidents waves to reflected ones are developed. The new approach consists in describing the wave relations in both spectral and spatial domains. The toggling between the spatial and spectral domain is ensured by the Discrete Angular Mathieu Transformation and its converse. The wave equations are solved using an iterative process in the presence of the excitation source. As a numerical example, we consider an infinite dielectric cylinder illuminated by a TM plane wave at an oblique incidence. The diffracted electric field is computed on both sides of the cylindrical surface as well as in the surrounding region for various incidence angles. The results obtained confirm the continuity conditions.

articleTitle: Two-Element Circularly Polarized Transparent MIMO Antenna for Sub-Six Wireless Communication Applications
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile proximity coupled transparent antenna is designed at 5.2GHz. A combination of materials is investigated. Plexiglass is the base material which has proven to provide high gain, low loss and high transparency. Circularly polarized transparent antenna is designed with FTO and plexiglass materials and 2-element MIMO antenna is then created. The diversity performance in terms of ECC and diversity gain is reported.

articleTitle: Measurement for Determination of Dielectric Material Permittivity Using Air-Host SIW Structure
abstract: This paper discusses the determination of dielectric material permittivity using an air-host substrate- integrated-waveguide (SIW) structure through measurement. The air-host SIW structure is made by a copper plate with the thickness of 0.45 mm for the SIW surface and the groundplane. It has the dimensions of 85 mm (length) x 38 mm (width) x 4.8 mm (height) with the cut-off frequency of 3.875 GHz for the fundamental TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> resonance mode. The material under test (MUT) used in the determination includes Arlon AD250A and FR-4 Epoxy dielectric substrates which takes a cylindrical shape with the dimensions of 18 mm (diameter) by 4.8 mm (height). The mechanism of measurement using the proposed air-host SIW structure is conducted by placing the MUT between the SIW surface and the groundplane. Based on the results, the accuracy for determining the dielectric material permittivity reaches up to 97.87 %.

articleTitle: High Performance RFID Temperature Sensor for IoT Applications
abstract: This paper presents a chipless RFID temperature sensor based on a slow-wave reflecting resonator using the RO3210 substrate that exhibits a dielectric constant with significant thermal coefficient. In addition to its temperature sensing functionality, the chipless sensor offers an impressive coding capacity of 8 bits in a frequency range of 8 to 12 GHz. This allows for the encoding and transmission of temperature data using the RFID technology. simulation results revealed a remarkable quality factor, coding stability and sensing precision that make it a reliable tool for temperature monitoring in various industries.

articleTitle: Microwave Sensors for Permittivity Measurement of Solid Materials
abstract: This paper focuses on the development and testing of microwave sensors for measuring the permittivity of solid materials. We developed a sensor utilizing two CSRR resonators in a CPW technology and tested it with a solid material of fixed height (6 mm) and permittivity values ranging from 2.0 to 2.8. By varying the permittivity within this range, we observed the S21 parameter to detect frequency shifts, allowing us to study how changes in permittivity affect the sensor's frequency response. The results revealed a clear relationship between the material's permittivity and the frequency shifts observed in the S21 parameter. By analyzing these shifts, we derived an equation relating permittivity to frequency. This relationship enables the identification of specific solid materials based on their permittivity, providing a reliable and non-invasive method for permittivity measurement in various applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Antenna Gain Using 2D- EBG Structures for C-Band Applications
abstract: This paper presents a novel Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) structure designed to enhance antenna performance. The proposed antenna features a rectangular patch fed by a 50 a SMA coaxial probe. The structure includes an innovative EBG rectangular box with four supports of Neltec NX9240 material, and its design and parametric analysis were conducted using Ansys HFSS simulation software. Utilizing a Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate with a relative permittivity of 2.2, this design significantly improves gain and reduces return losses. The proposed antenna achieves a gain of 12.60 dB and demonstrates substantial performance enhancements at the C-Band, particularly beneficial for radar and satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Broadband 0.1 – 18 GHz Transceiver
abstract: Working under DARPA's Digital RF Battlespace Emulator (DRBE) program we designed, tested, and delivered an ultra-wideband Radio Frequency (RF) transceiver to interface with a Real-Time High-Performance Computing (RT-HPC) to create the world's first, large scale, virtual RF environment for developing, training, and testing advanced RF systems. The transceiver module works in conjunction with the RT-HPC and Xilinx's Zynq UltraSCALE+ family of processors to both generate and receive complex waveforms to create a high-fidelity and very low latency RF test environment. The first generation of the RF transceiver has a 0.1 – 18 GHz overall Bandwidth (BW) with a 1 GHz Instantaneous Bandwidth (IBW). The outputs of the transmitter and receiver signal paths are designed to accommodate a wide range of Systems Under Test (SUT), varying signal amplitudes, while also maintaining high Spur Free Dynamic Range (SFDR). After testing and delivering the firstgeneration systems, we are currently developing the second generation of hardware aimed at increasing the IBW to 2 GHz and drastically lowering the Size, Weight, and Power (SWAP) requirements of the transceiver to enable DRBE to interface with an ever-increasing amount of SUTs simultaneously.

articleTitle: A Highly Linear and Efficient GaN RF Power Amplifier for Telemetry Applications in S-Band
abstract: This paper introduces a highly linear and efficient RF power amplifier (PA) for telemetry systems. The proposed in-phase parallel power amplifier is designed based on a developed algorithm to determine the optimum gate biases to provide high linearity with the best achievable efficiency. The measured saturated output power (Psat) is 44.9 dBm with power-added efficiency (PAE) of more than 61% and the 1-dB compression point is achieved at 44.4 dBm output power. The measured results showed good linearity with IM3 less than −46 dBc for the output power back-off (OBO) of 6 dB and 10 dB OBO. Furthermore, The adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) is − 27 dBc at an average output power of 42.3 dBm and an average power added efficiency of 53.5 %. The proposed design achieved competitive results compared to other published works.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of CMOS Fractional-N All-Digital Phase-Locked Loop (ADPLL)
abstract: A CMOS-based Charge-Pump PLL (CP-PLL) is designed and simulated using SPICE. A fractional-N All-Digital PLL (ADPLL) is designed using SystemVerilog and its VLSI layout is designed using a 35nm CMOS process and RTL-to-GDSII (logic-to-layout) synthesis. The CP-PLL simulations are contrasted to the ADPLL - the latter of which is subject to less undesirable effects such as low cutoff frequencies and RC delay. The approach presented shows how CMOS ADPLLs can be efficiently designed using RTL and logic-to-layout synthesis, to produce practical PLLs occupying a small die area, with a low power consumption, that can be implemented as part of a transceiver IC.

articleTitle: Design and Study of MIMO Antenna for WLAN Applications by Using DMS and DGS Techniques
abstract: This paper presents a new design of a compact MIMO antenna for WLAN applications. The proposed structure operate at 5.3 GHz band with high isolation. The proposed MIMO antenna is composed with two symmetrical radiating elements using microstrip technology. The structure incorporating defected microstrip structure (DMS) and defected Ground Structures (DGS) techniques to improve to performance at the desired frequency band in term of impedance bandwidth, isolation and efficiency. The simulated results show that the MIMO antenna has a high adaptation (S11 near to-40 dB) and high isolation (S12 around -30 dB) at the 5.3GHz. On the other hand, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and the diversity gain (DG) are less than 2.10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> and more than 9.99 dB at 5.3 GHz, respectively. Witch mean that, the proposed system has a good diversity gain at the WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Investigating Thermal Effects and Mitigation Strategies in Multi-Finger GaN HEMTs
abstract: Gallium Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors have garnered attention as promising solutions for high-power and high-frequency applications, attributed to their exceptional features such as high electron mobility, high breakdown voltage, and wide bandgap. However, the efficacy of GaN HEMTs is challenged by some restrictive phenomena, notably self-heating and thermal effects. This paper presents experimental results from DC analysis conducted on different GaN HEMT devices featuring various numbers of fingers, alongside an examination of the thermal impact on device performance. The correlation between finger count in multi-finger HEMTs and device performance is explored, followed by a discussion on mitigation strategies aimed at optimizing device design and structures to address these challenges.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication, and Validation of Printed Embedded Antennas
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design for a printed and composite embedded UHF RFID dipole antenna operating at 868 MHz. The goal of this paper is to design an antenna that enables reliable communication between an RFID tag embedded in fiberglass epoxy resin and a reader. The antenna is printed on a fiberglass layer using conductive inks and embedded within an epoxy-reinforced composite. The design process considers factors like resonance frequency and impedance matching to achieve efficient communication with an RFID chip. Simulations were conducted to optimize the design for the chosen material properties and chip impedance. The fabricated antenna achieves a reading distance of 2.1 meters, demonstrating its functionality. While the reading distance is shorter than commercial antennas, this design offers advantages such as integration within composite materials for external protection. It also has the potential to incorporate additional functionalities like printed sensors and energy harvesting in future iterations.

articleTitle: X/Ku Octave-Bandwidth Magic Tee for Satellite Communication
abstract: An Octave-Bandwidth Magic Tee with high performance is designed and constructed in this research. With a fractional bandwidth more than 66%, this circuit is based on two combined turnstile junction OMTs with 3 physical ports. When both OMTs combined through their circular common ports they result a Magic Tee with 4 ports in the band 8–16 GHz. The designed Magic-Tee exhibits a return loss better than 25 dB at any port and an isolation of 60 dB over the full bandwidth. This design can be used in applications of satellite communication, astronomy and radars thanks to its enhanced design, cost and performances regarding standard waveguide bands.

articleTitle: Signal-Interference Planar Bandpass Filters and Diplexers with Frequency-Symmetrical/Asymmetrical Stopband-Attenuation Profiles Using Filtering Cascading Networks
abstract: A family of transversal-signal-interference planar bandpass filters (BPFs) with frequency-symmetrical and asymmetrical filtering transfer functions is reported. These RF BPFs are shaped by two dissimilar bi-path in-parallel-transmission-line-based transversal filtering sections (TFSs) and a filtering cascading network to interconnect them. In this manner, overall high-selectivity BPF actions can be realized from the composition of the BPF response of the cascading network and the plurality of out-of-band transmission zeros (TZs) generated by the TFSs. For experimental-validation purposes, two proof-of-concept microstrip prototypes consisting of a 2-GHz frequency-symmetrical multi-TZ BPF and a 1.78/2.24-GHz sharp-rejection diplexer with spectrally-adjacent channels are designed, built, and measured.

articleTitle: Impact of Microwave Radiation Treatment on the Mortality and Fertility of the Wild Cochineal Dactylopius Opuntiae
abstract: Microwave radiation treatment has emerged as a potential method for controlling Dactylopius opuntiae, a pest infesting cactus pear. In this study, we investigated the efficacy of microwave radiation at 2.45 GHz against adult females of D. opuntiae, focusing on mortality rates and fertility outcomes. Our findings reveal that microwave radiation treatment led to 23% of mortalitty rate for adult D. opuntiae with wax. On the other hand, 100% mortality of adult D. opuntiae without wax, indicating a protective effect of wax against microwave radiation. Additionally, the results demonstrate a substantial impact on the fertility of D. opuntiae adults with wax, expressed by a significant reduction in the number of developed nymphs compared to untreated adults.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) Based on Coupled-Line Filters with a Notch Filter to Reject Unwanted Frequencies
abstract: In this article, we have designed a low-noise amplifier by optimizing its performance through the integration of line filters coupled at the input and output of the circuit, as well as a third notch filter for the suppression of undesirable frequencies. The obtained results conclusively confirm the unconditional stability of this amplifier over the entire frequency range from 2 to 3 GHz. Additionally, the gain achieved exceeds expectations, while the reflection coefficients at the input and output remain at minimum levels, essential to ensuring optimal amplifier performance. This amplifier design represents a versatile solution, ideal for integration into dedicated Wi-Fi systems, and offers promising prospects in areas such as wireless communications, wireless sensor technologies, telemetry systems, and remote monitoring devices. Using distributed elements, such as our filter, simplifies and makes the manufacturing process more cost-effective, requiring only two localized components, namely the resistor and the stability capacitor of our notch filter.

articleTitle: Low-profile Antenna Sensor Design and Implementation for Liquid Sensing Applications at 2.45GHz and 6.4GHz
abstract: In this paper, a detailed study has been performed to assess different techniques used for liquid sensing applications. Three different planar antennas have been designed at two different frequencies. The measuring technique is based on the amount of shift in resonance frequency upon changing the liquid sample. Different samples were assessed; with a dielectric relative permittivity that ranges between 1.9 and 80.4. An inset-fed patch antenna sensor was fabricated, where measured results of immersing the sensor in different samples agreed with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Dual-band MIMO Monopole Antenna for 4G and 5G Mobile Communication Devices
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of dual-band MIMO antennas for 4G and 5G mobile Sub-6GHz. The proposed antenna consists of an F-shaped monopole operating in the 3.6 GHz band, and a complementary slot of the same size as the F-shaped monopole to cover the 2.6 GHz and 3.6 GHz bands. A two-antenna array placed close to each other on the same FR4 epoxy substrate, measuring 120 × 60 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, equivalent in size to a modern mobile phone. To improve isolation between the two elements, the slot technique is implemented by creating a slot on the ground plane. S-parameters, radiation patterns, and MIMO parameters are presented to illustrate the performance of the MIMO antenna system. The design and simulation are carried out using HFSS software.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Gysel Combiner for C-Band High Power Applications
abstract: This paper presents an approach to enhance both the power handling capability and bandwidth of the Gysel combiner. The bandwidth is improved by varying the impedances while keeping a maximum impedance that ensures the required power handling and acceptable return loss. The design approach is demonstrated in a design operating within the 3–6 GHz frequency range, achieving octave fractional bandwidth and handling RF power up to 400 W in continuous wave operation. The topology of the proposed Gysel combiner features a compact form factor with dimensions of 39x36 mm.

articleTitle: Polarization Agile Frequency Selective Surface(FSS) for C, X and Ku Bands
abstract: To realize the concept of Co-Cross (LP-LP) and Cross-Circular (LP-CP) polarization of the reflected wave, a frequency selective surface (FSS) that is agile with respect to polarization across multiple bands (C, X, and Ku) is introduced. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${29\times 36}$</tex> FSS array acts as a polarization agile metasurface (MSF). It consists of a periodic single-layered split circular ring with rectangular slot and a diagonally rectangular strip that surrounds the half solid circular strips which behaves like a capacitor. The bottom layer of the proposed metasurface consists of a full copper ground structure that makes it a perfect reflector. The proposed FSS is able to add the Co-polarization to Cross-Polarization (LP-LP) and Cross-Polarization to Circular Polarization (LP-CP) capability. There is three Co-Pol to Cross-Pol bands are achieved from 7.3-7.7 GHz, 9.0-9.3 GHz, and 15.3-17 GHz. Similarly, for LP-CP, a mature band of 9.8-13 GHz having a fractional bandwidth of 28% is achieved. Furthermore, multiple useful operating bands and miniaturized single layer profile makes the proposed metasurface a potential candidate for polarization conversion useful applications.

articleTitle: High-Precision Satellite Position Interpolation: A Comparison of Lagrange, Cubic Spline, and Artificial Neural Network Methods
abstract: For advanced Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) applications like determining the bending angle in GNSS radio occultation, it is imperative to obtain high-precision satellite position estimates at millisecond intervals. This study evaluates Lagrange interpolation, cubic spline interpolation, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to achieve such high precision. Although both cubic spline interpolation and ANN are effective, ANN outperforms cubic spline interpolation with lower maximum errors and better handling of boundary conditions. In comparison, Lagrange interpolation demonstrates a lack of stability. ANN have been identified as the most effective technique for the accurate and continuous estimation of satellite positions through interpolation.

articleTitle: Continuous Wave Doppler Radar Occupant Count Estimation Using Spectral Features
abstract: Building occupancy estimation is important for efficient building management, energy consumption control, and occupant safety and well-being. Radar-based occupancy sensors have a potential to provide an effective tool for building occupancy monitoring, without privacy concerns inherent to camera use. In this paper we propose an occupant count approach based on spectral features of continuous wave Doppler radar signals in the presence of multiple occupants. The proposed approach is tested using envelope-transient simulation for the case of ten occupants, and it is demonstrated that spectral features change proportionally to the number of occupants.

articleTitle: Die Thickness - a Neglected Design Parameter
abstract: Electromagnetic interactions on-chip, at radio frequencies, are often unavoidable phenomena that designers must account for at the system level. While viable strategies to limit interference have been presented previously, the efficacy of die-thinning as a mitigation strategy has been underexplored in the available literature. Die-thinning is given focused attention in this work through a series of experiments with an electromagnetic simulator, where the passive structure of choice is the inductor. These simulations, conducted with EMX, demonstrated that for Q-value penalties of less than 30%, reductions in coupling by over two orders of magnitude are achievable. Additionally, the effects of an holistic approach, whereby separation, inductor topology, and die-thickness are optimized, is shown to yield coupling coefficients of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> or below for appropriate inductor geometries with realizable spacing constraints.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact Microstrip Triangular Open-Loop Bandpass Filter Using Meander Lines for WiFi 6E
abstract: This paper presents a compact microstrip bandpass filter for 6GHz, exhibiting excellent performance for Wi-Fi 6E. The aim of this work is to develop a triangular open-loop resonator utilizing a meander line to attain miniaturization. The present bandpass filter was designed using Advanced Design System software on Rogers RT5880 substrate. The simulation results indicate high performance with low insertion loss and good impedance matching. Furthermore, the proposed filter is well-miniaturized, occupying only 7.3 x 6.7 mm, which confirms the effectiveness of the meander line in reducing the structure's size.

articleTitle: Trapezoidal Antenna with Reconfigurable Frequency for Wireless Communication Systems
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile, trapezoidal-shaped, frequency-reconfigurable antenna, consisting of a trapezoidal radiating element surrounded by a 2 mm wide line and a rectangular ground plane with two L-shaped slots designed to operate in the microwave frequency band. The antenna is fed by a microstrip line. The substrate used is Rogers RT5880, with a relative permittivity of 2.2 and a tangent loss of 0.0009. To enable switching between different operating states, four PIN diodes are strategically inserted into the antenna's radiating top surface. The proposed Sub-6 GHz antenna operates in five states, covering six different frequency bands. The standing wave ratio (VSWR) of the presented antenna is less than 2 for all operating bands. The efficiency of the designed antenna is 90%, and the gain varies between 3 and 8.5 dBi across the corresponding operating frequency ranges. The proposed structure is simulated using the Computer Simulation Technology Microwave Studio (CST MWS) simulator. Due to its compact dimensions and compatibility with multiple wireless standards, including fourth and fifth-generation (5G) technology, the antenna is well-suited for integration into portable devices.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Octagonal Microstrip Patch Antenna Circularly Polarized for WIMAX and 5G Mid-Band Applications
abstract: In this paper, we present a new octagonal circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna that is suitable for applications such as WIMAX and 5G mid-band. We use a simple and efficient single-port excitation technique to achieve the desired result. The suggested antenna is printed on a Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate with a 2.2 relative permittivity and a low loss tangent (0.0009). Its optimum dimension is 32 × 35 × 1.67 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The square slot and stubs in the ground plane are utilized for generating circularly polarized radiation in the ground plane. The obtained bandwidth at -10 dB is from 2.87 GHz to 4 GHz (32.89%), and the axial ratio (AR) below 3 dB is within 3.31-3.69 GHz bandwidth (10.64%). All the obtained results are simulated using the tools (CST) and (HFSS). Our antenna has a compact size and is easy to construct; it has good performance, like a wide band in terms of a reflection coefficient equal to 1.13 GHz; and it is very adequate for mobile applications due to circular polarization, especially for WIMAX and 5G mid-band. This characteristic gives us more freedom to make it in any location.

articleTitle: Design and Study of a Bi-Band Antenna for WLAN and WiMAX Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dual-band microstrip patch antenna tailored for WLAN and WiMAX applications. The proposed compact antenna, featuring slits and slots, operates at three distinct frequencies: 3.45 GHz, 4.99 GHz, and 5.72 GHz. It achieves a return loss superior to -20dB at each of these frequencies, covering the lower band (3.38-3.54 GHz), and the upper band (4.76-6.38 GHz). The antenna exhibits bandwidths of 160 MHz, and 1620 MHz, for the respective bands, with VSWR values below 1.2, Constructed from FR4 material with a relative permittivity of 4.4 and a thickness of 1.6 mm, the antenna is fed using a microstrip feedline technique with a 50Ω impedance. The design and performance analyses are conducted using CST Microwave Studio software.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Phase-Difference Characteristics of Compact 4×4 Butler Matrix Structures
abstract: This paper presents the reconfigurable phase-difference characteristics of compact Butler matrix (BM) structures. The reconfigurable phase-difference characteristics are achieved by altering the phase-differences of couplers contained in the BM structure. For this case, capacitances are placed at the intersection of horizontal and vertical coupler arms. To implement the purpose, a 2.4 GHz 4×4 BM with reconfigurable phase-difference is simulated, fabricated, and measured. A Rogers RO4003C dielectric substrate is used for the design and realization. The proposed BM can produce reconfigurable phase-difference characteristics with the phase-difference range from −154°to 157°obtained by varying capacitances from 0.2 pF to 2.3 pF. Moreover, it has a compact size of 54.1 mm × 54.1 mm (0.43λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.43λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>).

articleTitle: Path Loss Prediction for V2I Communications Systems: A Performance Analysis of Propagation Models
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of path loss prediction models for V2I communication in urban environments, focusing on the impact of non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions. Field tests conducted in Bologna, Italy, provided a dataset encompassing four distinct NLOS scenarios. Linear regression and random forest (RF) models were trained and evaluated using meticulously prepared data. Our findings demonstrate the superior performance of the RF model in capturing complex data relationships, as evidenced by lower RMSE, MSE, and MAE values compared to both the linear regression and the standard 3GPP model. Furthermore, the application of a Kalman filter significantly enhanced the RF model's accuracy, achieving near-zero error levels in certain scenarios. In contrast, the 3GPP model exhibited limited improvement, revealing its inadequacy in accurately modeling path loss under complex urban conditions. This research underscores the potential of advanced machine learning techniques, like RF, combined with noise reduction strategies for achieving highly accurate and reliable path loss predictions for V2I communication systems.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for a Driver Power Amplifier with the Supply Modulation Concept
abstract: In this study, the design of a driver power amplifier with the supply modulation concept is investigated and realized. High-power amplifiers require significant input power at the peak power operation. To provide this specification, driver amplifiers, which directly affect the efficiency and linearity of the transmitter systems, are used as the input stage. Considering the composite power and spectral efficiencies of two-stage power amplifier modules, a deep Class-AB driver amplifier for the n78 5G band (3.3 – 3.8 GHz) is designed with a CGH40006P GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT). The driver power amplifier has an output power of 33.8 dBm at the 3-dB compression point, a small signal gain of 15.8 dB, and a power-added efficiency (PAE) of 68% at 3.5 GHz. Furthermore, the driver power amplifier demonstrates a PAE improvement of 10% with the supply-modulated operation.

articleTitle: A New Compact Cantor Set Fractal MIMO Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: This article outlines the development of a compact MIMO antenna with two ports crafted for millimeter-wave band operations, specifically tailored to support fifth-generation (5G) wireless applications. The suggested antenna is constructed on a Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate, measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${12} \times {6}\times {0.508} \text{mm}{3}$</tex>. The proposed antenna has a slotted ground on the bottom and two Fractal-shaped radiating elements inspired by the Cantor Set pattern, positioned atop the dielectric material. The suggested antenna covers the millimeter-wave spectrum utilized in 5G, showcasing a wide bandwidth extending from 26.6 GHz to 29.08 GHz and 38.5 to 39.2 GHz. The antenna attains a maximum gain of 7.64 dBi, robust isolation exceeding 26 dB and demonstrates exceptional diversity performance, with an envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) below 0.003 and a diversity gain (DG) surpassing 10 dB. The obtained results Confirm the validity of the designed MIMO antenna's robustness and make it a viable option for 5G wireless equipment.

articleTitle: Second-Order Quad-Band Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface with Multiple Transmission Zeros
abstract: This paper presents the design of an innovative second-order high-selectivity quad-band bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) with multiple close-to-passband transmission zeros (TZs). Its constituent unit cell comprises three metal elements, for which two identical metal patterns are printed on the top and bottom layers, and they are in a back-to-back configuration along with a middle-layer metal element in between. Meanwhile, two thin dielectric substrates are employed to separate these three metal layers. Based on the proposed design, the engineered FSS can attain a quad-band bandpass-filter (BPF) response. The four created transmission passbands are centered at 7.8, 12.3, 15.1, and 17.6 GHz, respectively, and their in-band power-reflection levels are higher than 10 dB. Due to the generated multiple stopband TZs located at the close-to-passband regions, sharp-rejection filtering capabilities for the proposed FSS are obtained. In addition, further merits of the conceived quad-band bandpass FSS are demonstrated, such as (i) its compact circuitry size, (ii) simple geometry of its building unit cell, and (iii) polarization-insensitive filtering response with high angular stability up to 30° incident angles for small variations of the bandwidths as confirmed at the electromagnetic-(EM)-simulation level.

articleTitle: Finger Width Effects on Performance of GaN HEMTs
abstract: In this study, we characterize GaN-HEMT devices and present both DC and AC measurement outcomes for the multi-finger configurations. Specifically, we introduce a new device featuring wide electrodes to assess and compare the performance of various multi-finger arrangements. This particular transistor comprises two fingers, each measuring 150 μm in width. We analyze and compare the s-parameters of structures with varying widths, extending our frequency range up to 67 GHz. This newly developed wide-finger configuration is integral to our ongoing efforts in developing optimized modeling approaches and improved transistor designs. The comparative analysis of different finger widths lays the groundwork for future explorations into high-frequency phenomena, including wave propagation effects and their impact on the performance of millimeter-wave transistors.
